title: とても～ない — “can't possibly ～”
summary: とても followed by a negative expression (usually the potential negative) means “absolutely cannot ～ / no way.” It strongly says that something is far beyond one's ability or reach. Typical endings are できない, 買えない, 無理だ.

patterns.form: とても ＋ 動詞可能形ない形（〜ない）
patterns.gloss: とても + potential negative (買えない, ついていけない)

patterns.form: とても ＋ 無理だ／不可能だ
patterns.gloss: とても + 無理だ / 不可能だ (a noun predicate that means impossible)

body.p: With a positive, とても means “very” (とても大きい). With a negative, it means “no matter what, impossible”: とても買えない. The negative form usually appears at the end of the sentence.
The potential negative (買えない, 食べられない, できない), 無理だ, 不可能だ, or ついていけない are common. It is a way to say “this is beyond me” and sounds strongly personal.
あまり〜ない means “not very ～” (a small degree). とても〜ない means a complete impossibility. They are different in strength.

examples.ja: そんな高（たか）い車（くるま）は、とても買（か）えない。
examples.romaji: Sonna takai kuruma wa, totemo kaenai.
examples.tr: I couldn't possibly buy such an expensive car.

examples.ja: この量（りょう）の仕事（しごと）を一日（いちにち）で終（お）えるのは、とても無理（むり）だ。
examples.romaji: Kono ryō no shigoto o ichinichi de oeru no wa, totemo muri da.
examples.tr: Finishing this much work in a single day is simply impossible.

examples.ja: あの人（ひと）の走（はし）る速（はや）さには、とてもついていけない。
examples.romaji: Ano hito no hashiru hayasa ni wa, totemo tsuite ikenai.
examples.tr: There's no way I can keep up with how fast that person runs.

pitfalls: Do not use it with a plain negative like 食べない. It needs a potential or impossible meaning: とても食べられない.
It is about your own ability or limit. Do not use it just for a simple dislike.
